Asserted on the named Match_addr column against an independent oracle, not on the presence of any string in the row. The fix, and the defect it closes, were captured at the wire through a logging proxy rather than inferred. ReverseGeocode makes TWO calls: one anonymous, which the server answered with the full address, and a second adding forStorage=true signed with the ArcGIS Online session token of the signed-in Pro seat. Honua is not that portal and never issued that token, and answered 498 Invalid Token - so the tool, which writes from the second response, wrote a row whose only populated columns were REV_InputX and REV_InputY, its own input. An endpoint that allows anonymous access is now served anonymously rather than refused: a caller presenting a token this server cannot validate is no better credentialed than one presenting none, and the endpoint already answers the latter. Endpoints that require authentication still answer 498/499. Two earlier server defects on this protocol closed the other geocode cells first: candidateFields not declaring the output schema (ERROR 000010) and resultId not echoing the submitted OBJECTID (0 Matched / 0 Unmatched over a 200 carrying a location).
